sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. Process mining 'aims at extracting process knowledge from so-called event logs', including hospital information systems, to 'discover, monitor and improve real processes'; 'there is often a significant gap between what is prescribed or supposed to happen' and what actually occurs; conformance checking detects deviations. The case's rework loop is the author's scenario.
Every organization, person, count and deadline is invented teaching data; tool output is an authored rendering in the tool style.

brief.situation: You analyze the emergency department's EHR event log at Riverside Regional Hospital (fictional). Since a new registration screen went live, median door-to-provider time rose from 24 to 41 minutes. The director plans to request another registration clerk at 11:00. It is 10:05. The event log is de-identified test data.
handover: The new screen made insurance fields mandatory before triage orders can be placed.
Event log: arrival, quick registration, triage, full registration, provider seen, with timestamps.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: look, change, check or ship. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

parts.label: What the log shows
parts.criteria: Process mining of the EHR event log reveals the real process: 38% of visits loop back to registration because insurance fields block triage orders; the queue has not grown, so it is rework (Lean waste), not a capacity problem.

parts.label: What you recommend
parts.criteria: Remove the cause by moving the fields after the provider and registering in parallel; a clerk speeds the waste; reminders shift it to nurses.
parts.modelAnswer: Move the fields; no new clerk.

parts.criteria: Replay last month's log now; re-mine the live log in two weeks and track door-to-provider.

scoring.modelReasoning: Door-to-provider rose after a screen change, not a volume change, so look at the real process. Mining the event log shows 38% of visits loop from triage back to registration because insurance fields now block triage orders, adding about 19 minutes, while the registration queue is unchanged. That is rework, a Lean waste, not a capacity gap. Move the fields after the provider, let registration finish in parallel, replay the log to confirm, and re-mine after two weeks. A clerk speeds the loop; reminders push clerical work to nurses.
